Does the guidance make sense for a student?

Start with a student’s story. Review the directions, the explanation, and the plan.

Share with caveats · Partial validation
Changes are live with this release. These fictional cases check plausibility. They do not establish reliability, predictive validity, fairness or industry certification.
12Different student stories
48Controlled changes to those stories
11Explicit career plans reviewed

What the stories caught

  • A visual interest could disappear. Liking visual layouts did not require liking music and writing. Narrower activity interests now remain visible.
  • Mixed fields could hide an interest. Disliking persuasion no longer suppresses accounting. Procedural healthcare stays visible for the student considering dentistry.
  • Three cards could repeat one interest. The set now balances connection strength with coverage of different liked activities. This is an editorial selection rule, not a validated ranking.
  • Broad answers could manufacture precision. Selecting everything no longer picks three arbitrary professions. Equal task connections stay tied. Conflicting earlier interests are explained.
  • A bookmark could skip unfinished questions. It now resumes at the missing question. Notes and completed work remain saved.

The student stories

Each uses uneven answers to individual activities, including dislikes and unfamiliar activities. Each was also tested with low confidence, little experience, higher lifestyle costs, and an education-loan payment scenario. None is an observed student or a population sample.

Physician · family medicine

Bachelor’s degree + MD or DO + family medicine residency

$70K before tax · First-year residency example. This is not pay immediately after high school.

Austin budget: Possible, with a little care.

  1. Explore a health question

    Use two reliable sources to explain a general health question. Notice whether you enjoy the science, explanation, or both. Use a public youth program for supervised exposure to healthcare.

  2. Map college, medical school, and residency

    Compare college prerequisites, four-year medical training, and family medicine residency. Budget each stage separately; no college major guarantees medical school admission.

  3. Ask about a normal day in family medicine

    Ask a physician and a resident about patient contact, documentation, training hours, and what they wish they knew in high school.

Earlier notes and completed work: preserved.

Independent six-interest pattern comparison for this chosen career: 0.89. Correlation is not an aptitude score or a probability.

Dentist · general dentistry

College prerequisites + DDS or DMD

$120K before tax · Estimated entry to the qualified role. This is not pay immediately after high school.

Austin budget: Room for the life you pictured.

  1. Try a safe hand-skills and design project

    Make a small clay model or detailed illustration. Notice precision, patience, and working with your hands. This is exploration, not a dental aptitude test.

  2. Map college prerequisites and dental school

    Compare college preparation, an accredited DDS/DMD, and Texas licensing. Include instruments, clinical fees, living costs, and possible loan payments.

  3. Ask a dentist about the everyday work

    Ask about patient anxiety, repetitive procedures, hand skills, employee pay, and the difference between practice revenue and take-home income.

Electricians

Electrical apprenticeship

$44K before tax · First-period apprenticeship example. This is not pay immediately after high school.

Austin budget: A few tradeoffs would help.

  1. Explore electrical work safely

    Visit a public training demonstration or approved student program. Practice algebra, measurement, and reading diagrams. Do not work on live wiring.

  2. Compare a paid apprenticeship and college options

    Austin ETA combines four years and 8,000 hours of training. Review admission steps, published pay, tuition, tools, and Texas licensing. Affordable technical or business college study can add options.

  3. Ask an apprentice and a qualified electrician

    Ask about hours, travel to job sites, physical demands, tuition, and how pay changes with completed training. Distinguish an employer schedule from the regional wage proxy.

How established tools compare

We reviewed O*NET’s six-interest profile method and CareerOneStop’s separate interest, skill and work-value tools. Similar themes do not make our original questionnaire equivalent to those instruments.

Live reference checkObserved O*NET result
Medicine exampleFamily physician, physician assistant and nurse practitioner: Best fit
Creative exampleGraphic designer: Best fit. Web/interface design and public relations were not returned for that profile.
Trades exampleElectrician, plumbing and HVAC: Best fit
Flat profileThe tool flags a flat profile and does not provide career matches.

We entered hypothetical six-score profiles through the official interface. We did not administer official questionnaires to these fictional students. The live comparisons use the three original walkthrough profiles; the twelve stories above have separate, local occupational-pattern comparisons.

Web/interface design can still appear when a student explicitly chooses interface tasks. That is a task-choice suggestion, not a claim that O*NET returned it. Generic visual choices no longer promote public relations.

Software coverage and reproducible evidence

These checks support software correctness, not the plausibility judgment by themselves.

  • All per-theme answer histograms
    All 3,003 histograms of ten answers over 1–5 and unfamiliar, separately for all six themes. Exact aggregate-score equivalence classes.
  • All theme-constant profiles
    All 46,656 combinations over six theme levels: 1–5 and unfamiliar. Actual production broad-suggestion function.
  • Every individual item response and unknown boundary
    60 items × six responses × six pure-theme baselines; independent mean/count oracle.
  • All feasible per-career question-support masks
    Every Boolean support pattern across the questions that can endorse each career; all eight questions explicitly answered or unsure. Exact career-level factorization, not every joint multiselect ranking.
  • Every multiselect subset within each question
    All local checkbox subsets, each tested against every career. Other questions unsure. Multiple options from one prompt must contribute at most one point.
  • All-select, unsure, incomplete and tie guards
    Every family: all-select, all-unsure and each missing follow-up. All reviewed careers retain direct plan reachability.
  • Confidence, money, work-preference and preservation independence
    All 24 practice/confidence states for each of 12 areas, income extremes; three different current plans.
  • Seeded heterogeneous full profiles
    10,000 reproducible full 60-item profiles plus random full multiselect answers; complete/uncertain/flat behavior and independent scoring oracle.
  • Independent O*NET occupational-profile comparison
    Pearson correlation over all six dimensions, without copying app field weights or branch scoring. Current official career-return method as benchmark, not a validation score.

Every reviewed career can still produce a plan. Occupational-pattern comparisons cover 116 of 117 catalog careers. Tattoo artist has no complete six-interest descriptor here and remains unbenchmarked.

The full cross-product is not enumerated. The finite spaces above were exhaustive within their stated boundaries; heterogeneous complete profiles were sampled.

Review scorecards

Totals count scoped components, not students or passed tests. “0 / N” means no remaining defects observed in that category; it does not mean every possible case was verified. The twelve stories informed repairs and are development cases, not an independent holdout sample.

Quality and usefulness

CategoryObserved defectsAssessment
Usefulness & completeness0 / 4Student stories, explanations, plans and external comparisons reviewed. Real-student outcome validation remains unavailable.
Analytical clarity0 / 3Interests, task choices and aptitude limits are separate. Ties and broad answers are explicit.
Visual & interaction consistency0 / 4Report, broad-answer view, conflicting-clue cards and resumed clinical follow-up checked. Other browser paths were sampled.

Analytical correctness and robustness

CategoryObserved defectsAssessment
Source authority & confidence0 / 3O*NET methodology; CareerOneStop skills and values design. Live CareerOneStop result agreement was not measured.
Scoring & value accuracy0 / 18Six interest-scale and twelve branch components; independent arithmetic and finite-space checks. Synthetic evidence only.
Within-chart agreementN/ANo quantitative charts in this review.
Complete source details0 / 4Four live O*NET comparison records retained, including the flat-profile result. Hypothetical score entry, not administered tests.
Cross-artifact consistency0 / 3Medicine, creative-work and trades examples reconciled with live reference results; differences retained.
Data-quality controls0 / 4Unknown, flat, multiple-selection and incomplete-follow-up rules checked.
Conclusion support0 / 4Interest suggestions, explicit career choice, no aptitude inference, and separation from money. Predictive validity and population fairness remain untested.

What still needs real students

Some secondary pathway cards remain broad. For example, analytical and safety interests can connect to healthcare or public-safety fields without indicating a desire to treat patients or respond to emergencies. Their follow-up answers must determine which work, if any, appeals.

Next: use new students and held-out stories, administer the unmodified official assessment alongside Fieldguide, review discrepancies with a qualified counselor, test stability over time, and check differences in reading level and exposure. Predefine the analysis before further tuning.

Skills and confidence are self-reported context. Values and work preferences are discussion prompts, not ranking weights. Aptitude is not measured. Salary and Austin budget calculations received regression checks; this review did not independently refresh every financial source.
